text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG is likely to post a fall in nine-month pre-tax profits on Thursday amid pressure on margins and rising costs, such as higher fuel expenses, analysts said on Wednesday.
"There is still significant pressure on its main airline business and the cargo business is not as it should be," Juergen Poellmann, an analyst at German bank Vereinsbank, said.
Analyst expectations focus on a pre-tax profit figure of between 440 and 460 million marks compared to the 506 million mark profit it made in the first nine months of last year.
Turnover is expected to rise around six percent to some 15 billion marks, analysts estimate.
Lufthansa is currently facing tough competition from cheap foreign rivals in its domestic market and is seeking to drive down its costs with a deep restructuring of its business.
It is also engaged in a pay dispute with the DAG white-collar union, which earlier this month organised stoppages that Lufthansa said cost it millions of marks.
One British-based analyst said he expected the nine-month figures, due around 0900 GMT, to show small improvements in the airline's capacity utilisation both in its passenger and cargo business.
But he added the improvements would be largely due to moves by the airline to cut its capacity rather than any increase in demand.

Uwe Weinreich, analyst at BHF-Bank, said increased fuel costs and personnel numbers would also weigh on profits, although other analysts noted that the airline had previously said 1996 fuel costs had been hedged on futures markets.
The relative weakness of the mark this year was seen as working in Lufthansa's favour after 1995, when the strength of the German currency hit the airline's profits hard.
